mcqs.q: What is the difference between inflectional and derivational morphology?
options: Inflectional morphemes mark grammatical features without changing word class (cat/cats, walk/walked); derivational morphemes create new words, often changing word class (happy → happiness, teach → teacher).
Inflectional morphology applies only to verbs and derivational only to nouns.
Voiced sounds use the lips; voiceless sounds use the tongue.
Inflection and derivation are two words for the same process.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between voiced and voiceless sounds?
options: Voiced sounds use the lips; voiceless sounds use the tongue.
Voiced sounds are loud and voiceless sounds are whispered.
Voiced sounds are produced with vocal-fold vibration (/b/, /d/, /g/, /z/); voiceless sounds without it (/p/, /t/, /k/, /s/). You can feel the difference by putting a hand on your throat.
Inflectional morphology applies only to verbs and derivational only to nouns.
